# Prune Deleted Subtasks From A Ticket's Embedded `## Subtasks` Checklist

## Goal

Make a parent ticket's locally-persisted `## Subtasks` checklist shrink when a subtask is
deleted on the remote, so the list an operator edits in the Tickets tab — and the list an
agent reads out of the local `.md` — matches what actually exists in the tracker.

### The problem

Every parent ticket imported into `.switchboard/tickets/<provider>/…` carries an
auto-generated block appended to its markdown body:

```
## Subtasks
<!-- generated by import — content below this line is not pushed to the remote ticket -->
- [ ] Wire the retry path (abc123) — backlog
- [x] Add the fixture (def456) — done
```

That block only ever **grows**. A subtask deleted in the tracker keeps its checklist line
forever. The operator sees the stale line whenever they open the ticket in the Tickets tab's
edit mode, and any agent handed the local `.md` as context plans against subtasks that no
longer exist.

### Root cause — three findings that compose

**1. `_mergeSubtasksSection` is additive-only, by design.**
`src/services/TaskViewerProvider.ts:23582`. It parses the existing block into an ordered
`id → entry-text` map, overwrites the slots the payload names, appends new ones, and
**preserves every slot the payload lacks**. Its own docstring states the rule and the reason:

```ts
 * A list payload is NEVER authoritative for a parent's complete subtask set:
 * ClickUp's `GET /list/{id}/task` only returns records whose *home list* is that
 * list … So a payload line replaces a matching line and a new line is appended,
 * but a line the payload lacks is PRESERVED. Deleted subtasks are reconciled only
 * by the per-open enrich (`importTaskAsDocument`, …).
```

The reasoning is correct. The problem is the reconciler it defers to.

**2. The reconciler it names is reachable in code, but every door into it is unsent.**

> **Superseded:** "The reconciler it names is never invoked… **nothing posts `importTicketSubtasks`.** Grepping the whole of `src/webview/` finds zero senders; the only other reference is a comment in `PlanningPanelProvider.ts:4812` recording that the arm was moved here. The verb is dead, so the merge's escape hatch never opens."
> **Reason:** The *conclusion* holds but the *reason* is too narrow, and the narrowness is what makes Change 5 below look safe when it is not. `importTaskAsDocument` is called from **six** sites, and three of them pass `includeSubtasks: true` — so the regenerating reconciler is not a single orphaned verb, it is a whole class of unsent doors. Deleting one of them does not shrink the class; it removes the only mechanism that can prune a line whose subtask has no local file.
> **Replaced with:** the audited call-site table below.

`importTaskAsDocument` (`TaskViewerProvider.ts:22422`) regenerates the block from scratch via
`_buildSubtasksSection` (22482 / 22511) and would prune correctly. Every caller that could
trigger that regeneration, audited:

| Caller | `includeSubtasks` | Live sender? |
|---|---|---|
| `importTicketSubtasks` (`TicketsPanelProvider.ts:3086`) | `true` | **No.** Zero `src/webview/` senders. Only other reference is the `PlanningPanelProvider.ts:4812` move comment. |
| `editTicket` (`TicketsPanelProvider.ts:2948`) | `true` | **No.** Zero `src/webview/` senders — a second dead door with the same shape. |
| `clickupImportTask` / `linearImportTask` (`TicketsPanelProvider.ts:3647` / `3612`) | from `msg` | **Only under `mode: 'document'`.** The one webview sender (`tickets.js:5540` → `handleTicketsImport(..., true, 'plan')`) passes `mode: 'plan'`, which routes to `switchboard.importClickUpTask` / `importLinearTask` instead. |
| `importAllTasks` slow path (`TaskViewerProvider.ts:24521`) | `true` | **No.** Needs `importMode: 'document'` **with** explicit `ids`; `tickets.js:5092` sends `tickets`/`asPlans`, never that pair. |
| `saveLocalTicketFile` (`TicketsPanelProvider.ts:2150`), ClickUp/Linear create (`3915` / `3994`) | `false` | n/a — cannot regenerate the block. |

So the block is never regenerated on any path a user can reach from the bundled webview.
It **is** reachable over HTTP — all of these are allowlisted verbs (`src/generated/verbAllowlist.ts`,
`TICKETS_VERBS`) served by `LocalApiServer` — which is exactly why Change 5 is now an
annotation rather than a deletion (see the Superseded callout there).

**3. The deletion sweep removes the subtask but not its line.**
`_applyConfirmedDeletions` (`TaskViewerProvider.ts:23900`) is the reconciler that *does*
run — it proves each candidate 404 against its own endpoint, unlinks the subtask's own
`.md`, and deletes its `imported_docs` row. It never opens the parent file. So the sidebar
correctly drops the deleted subtask while the parent's checklist still lists it — the exact
divergence being reported.

### The fix in one sentence

Hook the checklist rewrite onto the one path that already **proves** a ticket is gone: when
`_applyConfirmedDeletions` unlinks a subtask, drop that subtask's entry from its parent's
`## Subtasks` block.

This keeps the "a list payload is never authoritative" invariant intact — nothing is removed
on the strength of an absent payload record. A line is removed only when that specific
ticket's own endpoint returned 404.

### Known residual gap — what this fix deliberately does not reach

The hook is keyed on a **deletion candidate**, and a subtask only becomes a candidate if it
has an `imported_docs` row whose `file_path` sits in the swept directory
(`_collectDeletionCandidates:23787-23791`). The filesystem half of the nominator explicitly
`continue`s past any file carrying `parentId:` frontmatter (`23770-23775`), so subtasks are
nominated **from the DB only**. Two classes of checklist line therefore stay stale after this
change, by construction:

- **A subtask that never got a local file.** `importTaskAsDocument` writes the parent's
  checklist but no subtask files, so a cross-list ClickUp child (invisible to
  `GET /list/{id}/task` without `include_timl=true`) can hold a checklist line with nothing
  on disk to nominate.
- **An unregistered subtask file.** A file with no `imported_docs` row is invisible to the
  DB half and skipped by the FS half.

Both are pre-existing and out of scope. They are recorded here because they are the reason
the regenerating reconciler must not be deleted: it is the only mechanism that can ever
reach them, and wiring a sender to it is the natural follow-up plan.

## Metadata

- **Complexity:** 6
- **Tags:** bugfix, backend, reliability
- **Project:** Browser Switchboard

## User Review Required

- None.

## Complexity Audit

### Routine

- Reading a parent `.md`, slicing at `_SUBTASKS_HEADING`, and rewriting the tail. The exact
  slice-and-rewrite already exists at `TaskViewerProvider.ts:24254-24276` (the orphan-subtask
  upsert) and can be followed line for line.
- Re-stamping `last_synced_at` after the rewrite — also already written, at 24279-24285.
- Threading `provider` into `_applyConfirmedDeletions`. Two call sites (24394, 24472), both
  with `provider` already in scope from the destructure at 23960.

### Complex / Risky

- **The Linear checklist key is not the Linear deletion key.** `_buildSubtaskEntry:23471`
  writes `st.identifier` (`ENG-123`) into the parenthesised id slot for Linear, while a
  deletion candidate's `remoteId` is the issue **UUID** (`_normalizeLinearIssue:412` →
  `_writeTaskDocument` → `slugPrefix`/`remoteDocId`). An id-keyed `entries.delete()` is a
  silent no-op on every Linear subtask. This is the single defect most likely to ship green.
- **Restamping a locally-modified parent destroys the operator's edits.** The restamp clears
  the `modified` flag for the *whole file*, not just the block, so the next
  non-authoritative import stops skipping the parent and overwrites the user's unpushed
  title/description edits. The `## Subtasks` block carrying no pushable work does **not**
  license restamping the file that contains it.
- **Finding the parent of a deleted subtask.** The subtask's own file is being unlinked in
  the same pass, and its `parentId` lives in that file's frontmatter. The parent id must be
  captured **before** the unlink or it is gone.
- **Legacy checklist lines carry no id.** The shipped per-open enrich wrote ClickUp subtasks
  as `- [ ] ${name}` with no `(id)` suffix — `_parseSubtaskLine` (23521) keys those on
  `__title:<normalised title>`. An id-only prune silently misses every legacy line, and is
  also the only matcher that works for Linear until the identifier fix above lands.
- **Never destroy a line that is not provably dead.** A prune keyed on anything looser than
  a confirmed 404 id re-opens the cross-list data-loss the merge rule exists to prevent.

## Edge-Case & Dependency Audit

### Race Conditions

- **Sweep ordering within one import run.** The full sweep (24383-24400) runs *after* the
  per-item `_writeTaskDocument` loop, which has already merged the payload into the parent
  and restamped it. Our prune therefore rewrites a file written seconds earlier in the same
  run. That ordering is correct — the merge preserves the stale line (the deleted subtask is
  absent from the payload) and the prune removes it — but it means the parent is written
  twice per run and the second write must be the one that wins. Do not move the prune
  earlier.
- **Watcher churn.** Each parent rewrite fires the tickets file watcher. Batching by parent
  (one read + one write + one restamp) keeps this to one event per affected parent per
  sweep, not one per deleted child.
- **Concurrent panel edit.** An operator editing the parent in the Tickets tab while a
  background auto-sync (45s tick) prunes will have their in-flight textarea content
  clobbered on save-back. Same exposure as the existing orphan-subtask upsert at 24276;
  accepted, not newly introduced.

### Security

- No new network surface, no new user input parsed. All writes are to files already resolved
  through `_findTicketDocument`, which is DB-first and falls back to the same base dirs
  `_ticketBaseDirs` enumerates. The prune never constructs a path from remote data.
- The prune is strictly narrower than the unlink it accompanies: `_applyConfirmedDeletions`
  already enforces absolute-path and inside-`ticketsRoot` guards before deleting anything,
  and the prune only touches a parent that resolver returned.

### Side Effects

- **`last_synced_at` restamp** — see the Complex/Risky entry and edge case 6. Conditional.
- **Legacy blocks gain the generated-by-import marker.** Rewriting through
  `_SUBTASKS_HEADER` adds `<!-- generated by import … -->` to a pre-marker block that lacked
  it. This is the same normalisation `_mergeSubtasksSection` already performs and is
  desirable — it upgrades the block to the shape `stripAppendedBlocksForPush` recognises
  marker-first rather than by legacy shape-sniffing.
- **Parent mtime advances**, which is what makes the conditional restamp load-bearing.

### Dependencies & Conflicts

- `TaskViewerProvider._findTicketDocument` (22622) — DB-first parent resolution; already
  handles the renamed-parent case.
- `TaskViewerProvider._parseSubtaskEntries` / `_parseSubtaskLine` (23541 / 23521) — the only
  parser for checklist entries; reuse, do not re-implement.
- `TaskViewerProvider._SUBTASKS_HEADING` / `_SUBTASKS_HEADER` (23434 / 23435).
- `PlanningPanelCacheService.registerImportedTicket` (458) — signature is
  `(sourceId, docId, docName, slugPrefix, filePath, contentHash, workspaceId?, url?)`; the
  restamp must match the existing call shape at 24281-24284.
- `TicketDeletionCandidate` (154) — `{ remoteId, slugPrefix, paths, dbT }`. `remoteId` is
  already the id the prune needs; do **not** re-derive it from `slugPrefix`.
- **No conflict with the return-contract / parity / push-routing ratchets** — this change
  adds no verb, removes no verb (see Change 5), and adds no `postMessage`.

### Edge-case table

| # | Case | Required behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Parent file does not exist (never imported, or in another list's directory) | No-op. `_findTicketDocument` returns null → skip silently. |
| 2 | Parent has no `## Subtasks` block | No-op. `indexOf(_SUBTASKS_HEADING) === -1` → skip. Never create a block here. |
| 3 | Deleted subtask's line is the parent's **only** entry | The block collapses to empty. Write the parent with the heading removed entirely, not a bare header with zero entries — `_mergeSubtasksSection` already returns `''` for an empty map, so reuse that shape. |
| 4 | Legacy line with no `(id)` | Fall back to a title-key match: `__title:` + the deleted ticket's `docName`, normalised through `_parseSubtaskLine` so both sides go through the same parser. If neither key matches, leave the block untouched — a miss is acceptable, a wrong deletion is not. |
| 5 | Two subtasks with identical titles (legacy, no ids) | `_parseSubtaskEntries` suffixes colliding keys as `key#n`. A title-key prune must remove **at most one** slot, and only when exactly one candidate matches; ambiguous → leave alone. |
| 6 | Parent is locally modified (mtime > `last_synced_at` + 1s) | Still prune — the block is excluded from every push (`stripAppendedBlocksForPush`, `ticketDisplayContent.ts:61`) so it can carry no unpushed user work. **Do NOT restamp.** See the Superseded callout on this row below. |
| 7 | Several subtasks of the same parent deleted in one sweep | Batch by parent: read once, remove all matching slots, write once. A per-subtask read/write loop restamps repeatedly and multiplies watcher churn. |
| 8 | Parent and subtask both deleted in the same sweep | The parent file is gone by the time the prune runs. Case 1 handles it; do not resurrect a parent file. |
| 9 | Deletion sweep runs on the delta path (`TaskViewerProvider.ts:24429`) | Same treatment. Both sweeps funnel through `_applyConfirmedDeletions`, so hooking there covers full and delta identically — which is the point of hooking there rather than in `importAllTasks`' full-only prune. |
| 10 | Write fails (read-only FS, permissions) | Log and continue. A failed checklist rewrite must never abort the sweep or fail the import; the subtask file has already been unlinked. |
| 11 | **Linear subtask** — checklist id is `ENG-123`, candidate id is a UUID | Match on the identifier recovered from the stored issue URL, then fall back to the title key. An id-only match is a guaranteed miss. See Change 2. |
| 12 | Deleted subtask has a checklist line but no local file / no `imported_docs` row | Not reachable — it never becomes a deletion candidate. Documented in "Known residual gap"; explicitly out of scope. |
| 13 | Parent block uses `\n## Subtasks\n` (single leading newline) or CRLF | No-op. `indexOf(_SUBTASKS_HEADING)` requires the exact `\n\n## Subtasks\n`. Same limitation as every existing consumer (23649, 24255); do not "improve" it here — a looser match in a *destructive* path is not the place to relax a guard that a read path tolerates. |

> **Superseded (edge case 6):** "Still prune. … but restamp afterwards so the parent does not become permanently 'modified' and start being skipped by imports."
> **Reason:** The restamp does not scope to the block — it clears the `modified` verdict for the entire file. A parent whose *description* carries unpushed operator edits is protected only by that verdict (`importAllTasks` conflict guard, 24135-24151). Restamping it hands the next background delta permission to overwrite those edits. The stated justification ("the block can carry no unpushed user work") licenses rewriting the block; it does not license clearing the flag that protects everything above it. A parent that was already `modified` before the prune stays `modified` after it — that is not a regression, it is the pre-existing and correct state.
> **Replaced with:** capture `wasModified` (mtime > `last_synced_at` + 1000ms, matching the 1s grace used everywhere else) **before** the write; restamp **only** when the parent was synced. Never restamp a parent that was already modified.

**Not in scope / deliberately unchanged**

- `_mergeSubtasksSection`'s preserve-on-absence rule stays exactly as it is. Only the
  docstring's claim about who reconciles deletions changes.
- Local subtask **files** are already reconciled — the sweep unlinks them and
  `importAllTasks`' prune (24310-24355) spares them from the keep-set logic. Nothing here
  touches that.
- The detail pane's live Subtasks nav (`src/webview/tickets.js:773`) and the sidebar
  drill-down both render `linear.getSubtasks()` / `getTaskDetails().subtasks` — live remote
  data, already correct.
- `_collectDeletionCandidates`' `parentId:` skip (23770-23775) stays. Widening nomination to
  cover unregistered subtask files changes what the sweep may delete, which is a different
  and far riskier change than what this plan is for.

## Dependencies

- None. No prior session's work is required and nothing here blocks on another plan.

## Adversarial Synthesis

**Risk summary.** Three failure modes dominate: a Linear-only silent no-op (the checklist
keys on `identifier`, the sweep keys on the UUID — an id-keyed delete never fires and every
gate stays green), destruction of an operator's unpushed parent-file edits if the
`last_synced_at` restamp is unconditional, and a stale-`parentId` capture if the frontmatter
is read after the unlink rather than before. Mitigations: an id-first / identifier-second /
title-key-third matcher with a strict single-match rule, a `wasModified` probe taken before
the write that suppresses the restamp for already-modified parents, and capturing the
frontmatter inside `_applyConfirmedDeletions` immediately before `fs.promises.unlink`. The
change is additive to a path that already proves each deletion against its own endpoint, so
the "never delete a line that isn't provably dead" invariant is structurally preserved
rather than merely asserted.

## Proposed Changes

### 1. `src/services/TaskViewerProvider.ts` — capture parent id + identifier before the unlink

> **Superseded:** "`_collectDeletionCandidates` builds the `TicketDeletionCandidate` records. Read each candidate file's `parentId:` frontmatter there (the file still exists at that point) and carry it on the record" — adding `parentId?` / `docName?` to `TicketDeletionCandidate`.
> **Reason:** Wrong function, and the placement does not work as written. `_collectDeletionCandidates` has two nominating branches: the filesystem branch **`continue`s past every file with `parentId:` frontmatter** (23770-23775), so there is nothing to capture there; and the DB branch (23787-23791) never opens a file at all. Beyond that, nomination is far wider than confirmation — the probe cap is 25 (`_DELETION_PROBE_CAP:23719`) but nomination routinely produces hundreds of candidates, so reading frontmatter at nomination time is I/O for files that will never be deleted. It also introduces the exact "captured before the unlink or it is gone" hazard the plan then has to defend against.
> **Replaced with:** capture inside `_applyConfirmedDeletions`, immediately before the unlink loop for that candidate. The file is guaranteed present (we are about to delete it), the read happens only for confirmed-404 tickets, `TicketDeletionCandidate` needs no new fields, and `_collectDeletionCandidates` is not touched at all.

**Context.** `_applyConfirmedDeletions` (23900) already iterates `candidate.paths` and unlinks
each. The subtask's `parentId` frontmatter is readable right up to that unlink.

**Logic.** For each confirmed candidate, read the first readable path's frontmatter *before*
unlinking; if it carries `parentId:`, record `{ id, parentId, docName, identifier }` for the
post-loop prune. `docName` and `url` come from `candidate.dbT` (non-null for every subtask
candidate, since the FS branch cannot nominate one).

**Implementation.**

```ts
// Inside the `for (const candidate of confirmed)` loop, BEFORE the unlink loop:
let parentId = '';
for (const filePath of candidate.paths) {
    try {
        const fm = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8').slice(0, 4096).match(/^---\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n---/);
        const pm = fm && fm[1].match(/^parentId:\s*(.+)$/m);
        if (pm) { parentId = pm[1].trim(); break; }
    } catch { /* unreadable — try the next known copy */ }
}
```

and after `removed++`:

```ts
if (parentId) {
    unlinkedChildren.push({
        id: candidate.remoteId,
        parentId,
        docName: candidate.dbT?.docName || undefined,
        identifier: provider === 'linear'
            ? TaskViewerProvider._linearIdentifierFromUrl(candidate.dbT?.url)
            : ''
    });
}
```

**Edge cases.** Unreadable / already-gone file → no `parentId` → the child is simply not
pruned (edge case 10). No frontmatter, or frontmatter without `parentId:` → this was a
top-level ticket, not a subtask; skip. 4096-byte slice matches the intent of the 2048-byte
head probe at 23773 with headroom for a fuller ClickUp frontmatter block (status, listId,
priority, assignees).

### 2. `src/services/TaskViewerProvider.ts` — new `_pruneSubtaskLinesFromParents`

**Context.** New private method on `TaskViewerProvider`, placed next to `_applyConfirmedDeletions`.
It is the only caller-visible new surface in this change.

**Logic.** Batch the confirmed-deleted children by parent (edge case 7). Per parent: resolve
the file, slice at the heading, parse with the shared parser, delete one slot per child using
an id-first / identifier-second / title-key-third matcher, rebuild through the same producer
shape `_mergeSubtasksSection` uses, write once, and restamp **only if the parent was not
already locally modified**.

> **Superseded:** the id-only match `if (entries.delete(child.id)) { removedHere++; continue; }`, with a title-key fallback reached only when `child.id` misses.
> **Reason:** For Linear this never matches. `_buildSubtaskEntry:23471` writes `idStr = String(st?.identifier || st?.id)` — the human identifier `ENG-123` — into the checklist's `(…)` slot, while `TicketDeletionCandidate.remoteId` is the issue UUID (`_normalizeLinearIssue:412` sets `parentId` from `raw.parent.id`; `_writeTaskDocument` keys `slugPrefix` on `issue.id`; `fetchAllIssueIds` collects `node.id`). So every Linear prune would fall through to the title key by accident rather than by design — silently, with the whole test suite green, which is precisely the failure class this plan exists to close. It also re-derived the id as `candidate.dbT?.remoteDocId || candidate.slugPrefix.replace(/^[a-z]+_/, '')` when `candidate.remoteId` is the field that already holds it.
> **Replaced with:** an explicit ordered key list per child — `[id, identifier]` tried as exact/`#n`-suffixed slot matches first, then the title key — resolved through one shared helper, with a strict single-match rule at every step.

**Implementation.**

```ts
/**
 * Linear checklist lines key on the ISSUE IDENTIFIER (`ENG-123`), which
 * _buildSubtaskEntry writes into the `(…)` slot — NOT the UUID the deletion sweep
 * carries. The identifier is recoverable from the issue URL persisted on the
 * imported_docs row. ClickUp needs none of this: its checklist id IS its task id.
 */
private static _linearIdentifierFromUrl(url: string | undefined): string {
    const m = String(url || '').match(/\/issue\/([A-Za-z0-9]+-\d+)(?:[/?#]|$)/);
    return m ? m[1] : '';
}

/**
 * Delete at most ONE slot matching any of `keys`, in order. A key matches a slot
 * exactly, or as `key#n` (the collision suffix _parseSubtaskEntries applies to two
 * lines sharing a key). Ambiguity — two slots matching the same key — removes
 * nothing: a miss is acceptable, a wrong deletion is not (edge case 5).
 */
private _deleteOneMatchingSlot(entries: Map<string, string>, keys: string[]): boolean {
    for (const key of keys) {
        if (!key) { continue; }
        const matches = [...entries.keys()].filter(k => k === key || k.startsWith(`${key}#`));
        if (matches.length === 1) { entries.delete(matches[0]); return true; }
    }
    return false;
}

/**
 * Remove confirmed-deleted subtasks from their parents' `## Subtasks` checklists.
 *
 * Called ONLY from _applyConfirmedDeletions, and only for tickets whose own endpoint
 * returned 404. That proof is what makes removal safe here while _mergeSubtasksSection
 * still (correctly) preserves lines a list payload merely omits — a payload's silence
 * is not evidence, a 404 is.
 */
private async _pruneSubtaskLinesFromParents(
    resolvedRoot: string,
    provider: 'linear' | 'clickup',
    deleted: Array<{ id: string; parentId: string; docName?: string; identifier?: string }>
): Promise<number> {
    // Batch by parent (edge case 7): one read + one write + one restamp per parent.
    const byParent = new Map<string, Array<{ id: string; docName?: string; identifier?: string }>>();
    for (const d of deleted) {
        if (!d.parentId || !d.id) { continue; }
        const list = byParent.get(d.parentId) || [];
        list.push({ id: d.id, docName: d.docName, identifier: d.identifier });
        byParent.set(d.parentId, list);
    }
    if (byParent.size === 0) { return 0; }

    // Hoisted: one cache handle and ONE getImportedTickets() query for the whole
    // pass. Querying per parent inside the loop is a full table read per affected
    // parent, which is exactly the churn edge case 7 exists to avoid.
    const cacheService = this._getCacheService(resolvedRoot);
    let dbTickets: any[] = [];
    try { dbTickets = await cacheService.getImportedTickets(); } catch { /* restamp becomes a no-op */ }

    let pruned = 0;
    for (const [parentId, children] of byParent) {
        try {
            const parentFile = await this._findTicketDocument(resolvedRoot, provider, parentId);
            if (!parentFile || !fs.existsSync(parentFile)) { continue; }          // edge case 1 / 8
            const parentContent = fs.readFileSync(parentFile, 'utf8');
            const headingIdx = parentContent.indexOf(TaskViewerProvider._SUBTASKS_HEADING);
            if (headingIdx === -1) { continue; }                                   // edge cases 2 / 13

            const dbEntry = dbTickets.find((t: any) => t.slugPrefix === `${provider}_${parentId}`);
            // Probe BEFORE the write — afterwards our own mtime makes every parent
            // look modified. Same 1s grace as the conflict guard at 24145.
            let wasModified = false;
            if (dbEntry && dbEntry.lastSyncedAt) {
                try {
                    wasModified = fs.statSync(parentFile).mtimeMs
                        > new Date(dbEntry.lastSyncedAt).getTime() + 1000;
                } catch { /* treat as synced */ }
            }

            const entries = this._parseSubtaskEntries(parentContent.slice(headingIdx));
            let removedHere = 0;
            for (const child of children) {
                // id → identifier → title key. The first two are exact and
                // unambiguous; the title key is the legacy / identifier-less
                // fallback (edge cases 4, 5, 11).
                const keys = [child.id, child.identifier || ''];
                if (child.docName) {
                    keys.push(this._parseSubtaskLine(`- [ ] ${child.docName}`).titleKey);
                }
                if (this._deleteOneMatchingSlot(entries, keys)) { removedHere++; }
            }
            if (removedHere === 0) { continue; }

            // Rebuild through the same producer shape _mergeSubtasksSection uses, so an
            // emptied map collapses the block instead of leaving a bare header
            // (edge case 3).
            let section = '';
            if (entries.size > 0) {
                section = TaskViewerProvider._SUBTASKS_HEADER;
                for (const text of entries.values()) { section += `\n${text}`; }
            }
            fs.writeFileSync(parentFile, parentContent.slice(0, headingIdx) + section, 'utf8');
            pruned += removedHere;

            // Restamp ONLY a parent that was synced before this rewrite, or the
            // restamp clears the `modified` verdict that is the sole protection for
            // the operator's unpushed edits ABOVE the block (edge case 6).
            if (dbEntry && !wasModified) {
                await cacheService.registerImportedTicket(
                    provider, parentId, dbEntry.docName, dbEntry.slugPrefix,
                    parentFile, '', undefined, dbEntry.url
                );
            }
        } catch (e) {
            // Never abort the sweep for a checklist rewrite (edge case 10).
            console.warn(`[TaskViewerProvider] subtask-line prune failed for parent ${parentId}:`, e);
        }
    }
    return pruned;
}
```

**Edge cases.** Covered inline above: 1/8 (missing parent), 2/13 (no block, or a block whose
heading does not match the exact `\n\n## Subtasks\n` sentinel), 3 (block collapses), 4/5/11
(matcher order and single-match rule), 6 (conditional restamp), 7 (batching + hoisted query),
10 (per-parent try/catch).

### 3. `src/services/TaskViewerProvider.ts` — call it from `_applyConfirmedDeletions`

**Context.** `_applyConfirmedDeletions` (23900) currently takes
`(resolvedRoot, ticketsRoot, confirmed, logLabel)` and has exactly two callers: the full
sweep at 24394 and the delta sweep at 24472. Both have `provider` in scope from the
destructure at 23960.

**Logic.** Add a `provider` parameter, collect the successfully-unlinked candidates that had
a `parentId`, and prune once after the loop.

**Implementation.**

```ts
private async _applyConfirmedDeletions(
    resolvedRoot: string,
    ticketsRoot: string | undefined,
    confirmed: TicketDeletionCandidate[],
    logLabel: string,
    provider: 'linear' | 'clickup'
): Promise<number> {
    …
    const unlinkedChildren: Array<{ id: string; parentId: string; docName?: string; identifier?: string }> = [];
    for (const candidate of confirmed) {
        // …Change 1's frontmatter capture goes here, before the unlink loop…
        …
        if (!unlinkedAny) { continue; }
        …
        removed++;
        if (parentId) {
            unlinkedChildren.push({
                id: candidate.remoteId,
                parentId,
                docName: candidate.dbT?.docName || undefined,
                identifier: provider === 'linear'
                    ? TaskViewerProvider._linearIdentifierFromUrl(candidate.dbT?.url)
                    : ''
            });
        }
    }
    if (unlinkedChildren.length > 0) {
        const lines = await this._pruneSubtaskLinesFromParents(
            resolvedRoot, provider, unlinkedChildren
        );
        if (lines > 0) {
            console.log(`[TaskViewerProvider] ${logLabel}: pruned ${lines} stale subtask line(s) from parent checklists`);
        }
    }
    return removed;
}
```

Update both call sites to pass `provider`:

```ts
// 24394 (full sweep)
deletedCount += await this._applyConfirmedDeletions(resolvedRoot, ticketsRoot, confirmed, 'Deletion sweep', provider);
// 24472 (delta sweep)
deletedCount += await this._applyConfirmedDeletions(resolvedRoot, ticketsRoot, confirmed, 'Deletion sweep (delta)', provider);
```

Thread it as a parameter rather than re-deriving it from a slug prefix — the callers already
hold the typed value.

**Edge cases.** `confirmed.length === 0` still short-circuits at the top of the method, so the
prune costs nothing on the overwhelmingly common no-deletions path.

### 4. `src/services/TaskViewerProvider.ts` — correct the `_mergeSubtasksSection` docstring

**Context.** `23574-23581`. The rule stays; the sentence naming the reconciler is now false
and is what hid this bug through four reviews.

+ * lacks is PRESERVED. Deletions are reconciled by the deletion sweep instead:

### 5. `src/services/TicketsPanelProvider.ts` — annotate the unsent `importTicketSubtasks` arm

> **Superseded:** "delete the dead `importTicketSubtasks` arm. `TicketsPanelProvider.ts:3086-3136` has no sender anywhere in `src/webview/`. … Remove the `case` block."
> **Reason:** Three things make deletion the wrong trade. (a) It is not dead — it is an **allowlisted HTTP verb** (`src/generated/verbAllowlist.ts`, `TICKETS_VERBS`) served by `LocalApiServer` to the browser cockpit and any external orchestrator, on ~4,000 installs; "no sender in `src/webview/`" is evidence about the bundled webview, not about callers. (b) It is the **only** mechanism that can prune the two line-classes this plan provably cannot reach (see "Known residual gap") — deleting it locks that gap in permanently and makes the natural follow-up (wire a sender) strictly harder. (c) The cost is real and buys nothing: regenerating `src/generated/verbAllowlist.ts`, editing three `protocol-catalog.json` entries (1711, 1998, 5237), deleting `src/test/verb-engine-tickets-headless.test.js:252` and `src/test/tickets-subtask-embedding.test.js:350-364`, and re-running `npm run parity:check`. The stated benefit — "its presence is why the gap read as covered in four reviews" — is delivered by Change 4's docstring correction, not by deletion. Deleting a working reconciler to stop a *comment* from lying is the wrong half of the pair to remove.
> **Replaced with:** leave the arm and its tests intact; add a comment stating plainly that it has no bundled-webview sender and is HTTP-reachable only, so the next reader cannot mistake it for a live per-open enrich.

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests

Extend `src/test/tickets-subtask-embedding.test.js`, which already covers the merge and strip
helpers:

1. `_pruneSubtaskLinesFromParents` removes an id-keyed ClickUp line and leaves every sibling
   byte-identical.
2. **Linear identifier match (edge case 11):** a parent whose checklist line reads
   `- [ ] Wire retry (ENG-42) — Todo` is pruned when the deleted candidate carries the issue
   **UUID** plus `url: https://linear.app/acme/issue/ENG-42/wire-retry`. Assert it is
   removed. This test must fail against an id-only matcher — it is the regression guard for
   the defect that would otherwise ship green.
3. `_linearIdentifierFromUrl` returns `ENG-42` for the canonical URL, `''` for an empty /
   malformed / non-Linear URL, and does not match a trailing path segment that is not an
   identifier.
4. Legacy line with no `(id)`: removed via the title-key fallback when exactly one slot
   matches; **left in place** when two slots share the title (edge case 5).
5. Removing the last entry collapses the whole block — the written file contains no
   `## Subtasks` heading and no trailing header comment (edge case 3).
6. Parent with no block, and parent file absent: both no-op, no throw, no file created
   (edge cases 1 and 2).
7. Two children of one parent deleted in one call → exactly one `writeFileSync` for that
   parent (edge case 7), asserted on a stubbed `fs`.
8. **Restamp is conditional (edge case 6):** with a stubbed cache service, a parent whose
   mtime exceeds `last_synced_at + 1000` is still pruned but `registerImportedTicket` is
   **not** called; a synced parent is pruned **and** restamped. Both directions asserted —
   this is the data-loss guard.
9. `_applyConfirmedDeletions` reads `parentId:` frontmatter **before** `unlink`: assert on a
   stubbed `fs` that the read for a given path precedes its unlink, and that a candidate
   whose file has no `parentId:` contributes nothing to the prune.
10. Regression guard: `_mergeSubtasksSection` still preserves a line absent from the payload.
    This is the invariant the change must not break, and the test must fail loudly if a later
    "simplification" makes the merge authoritative.
11. Source assertion that `_applyConfirmedDeletions` is called with a `provider` argument at
    both sweep sites (24394, 24472) — a missed call site is a TypeScript error today but a
    silent wrong-provider bug if the parameter is ever made optional.

Existing tests that must keep passing unchanged (Change 5 no longer removes them):
`src/test/tickets-subtask-embedding.test.js:350-364` (the `importTicketSubtasks` restamp
assertion) and `src/test/verb-engine-tickets-headless.test.js:252` (the in-body return
contract for that verb).

### Manual (VSIX)

The shipped build, not `dist/`.

1. Import a ClickUp parent with three subtasks. Confirm the local parent `.md` carries all
   three under `## Subtasks`.
2. Delete one subtask in ClickUp.
3. Hit Refresh in the Tickets tab (delta path) and confirm from the extension log that the
   delta deletion sweep confirmed the 404 and logged `pruned N stale subtask line(s)`.
4. Open the parent `.md` on disk: the deleted subtask's line is gone, the other two are
   byte-identical, and the block's header comment is intact.
5. Open the parent in the Tickets tab and click into edit mode — the textarea shows two
   subtasks, not three.
6. Confirm the parent's sidebar sync badge still reads **synced**, not **modified** (the
   restamp worked).
7. **Modified-parent guard:** edit a *different* parent's description locally (do not push),
   confirm its badge reads **modified**, delete one of its subtasks remotely, Refresh. The
   subtask's line must be gone **and** the badge must still read **modified** — and the local
   description edit must survive the next Refresh.
8. **Linear:** repeat steps 1-6 against a Linear project with sub-issues. This is the path
   an id-only matcher silently no-ops, so it must be exercised explicitly, not assumed
   symmetric with ClickUp.
9. Repeat with a full Refetch (authoritative path) to confirm both sweeps behave identically.
10. Delete a subtask whose parent lives in a different list directory — confirm the parent is
    still found (DB-first resolution) and pruned.
